Narrow task 210 permanently to the mechanical routing fix already landed: keep exclusion's regression coverage, mark logos/imposition's TestGenericPinningReachesRebuiltSolve parametrizations xfail with the blocking reason cited, and accept a reduced Done-when scope for this task

errors.message: TestGenericPinningReachesRebuiltSolve fails for logos and imposition (all intercepted rebuilds return None/UNSAT) because the live search's persistent solver is empty (0 assertions) for these theories -- a separate, pre-existing defect in models/structure.py's solve()/ConstraintGenerator.stored_solver fallback, confirmed for logos, exclusion, and imposition alike, not introduced by this task's own fix.
errors.recommendation: See user_decision above. The fix itself (routing pins into frame_constraints) is correct, committed, and already verified working for exclusion; the blocker is a separate defect outside this task's declared scope.

memory_candidates.content: models/structure.py's solve() unconditionally clears model_structure.solver in a finally block for every theory (not just bimodal), and ConstraintGenerator._create_persistent_solver's stored_solver fallback always points at the pre-population (empty) solver -- so iterate/constraints.py's persistent search solver is empty (0 assertions) at construction for every theory. This means live iterate:N>1 search candidates for logos/exclusion/imposition are not actually constrained by real semantics during the search itself, only by whatever bit-difference exclusion clause is added -- verify with len(iterator.constraint_generator.solver.assertions()) == 0 immediately after constructing any theory's ModelIterator against a real, solved BuildExample. Bimodal already works around this for itself via _ensure_frame_constraints_in_search_solver; the same fix has never been generalized.

z3.Function(name, ...) and z3.BitVec(name, ...) declarations with the same name+signature are interned within the same Z3 context, even across separate Python-object constructions -- so cross-instance pinning (evaluating a fresh semantics instance's Z3 term against a Z3 model produced by a different, earlier semantics instance) works correctly as long as names/sorts match. This is what makes the generic iterator pinning loop's cross-instance eval technique sound.
